Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review

input.description: Find GraphQL or public API schema
input.prompt:
Investigate this repository at /bench/repo to answer: Where is the GraphQL schema for the public API defined?

I suspect the premise may be wrong (there may be no GraphQL at all — could be REST/OpenAPI/tRPC instead). Search thoroughly:
- Look for any GraphQL usage: *.graphql, *.gql files, `type Query`, `gql\`\``, apollo, graphql-js, schema.graphql, buildSchema, makeExecutableSchema, TypeDefs
- Look for how the public API is actually defined: REST routes, OpenAPI/Swagger specs, tRPC routers, controllers, API directories
- Check package.json dependencies for graphql-related packages vs REST frameworks

Report: (1) whether GraphQL exists at all, (2) what the actual public API surface is and where it's defined, with concrete file paths. Give exact file paths and evidence.

content.text:
I have enough to give a definitive answer.

## Answer

**(1) Does GraphQL exist? No.** There is zero GraphQL in this repository. Searches for `*.graphql`/`*.gql` files, and for `type Query`, `gql\`\``, `apollo`, `makeExecutableSchema`, `buildSchema`, `typeDefs`, `ApolloServer`, etc. across all Go/JS/TS files returned nothing. There are no graphql packages in `go.mod` or `web/package.json`. The premise is incorrect.

**(2) What the public API actually is: Protocol Buffers → gRPC + REST gateway + Connect, with a generated OpenAPI spec.**

This is the **Memos** project (open-source note-taking tool, Go backend). The public API "schema" is defined in **`.proto` (Protocol Buffer) files**, not GraphQL/OpenAPI-authored/tRPC. The README itself states: *"full REST and gRPC APIs for integration."*

Where the API schema is defined:
- **`/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/*.proto`** — the source of truth for the public API. Service definitions:
  - `/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/memo_service.proto`
  - `/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/user_service.proto`
  - `/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/auth_service.proto`
  - `/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/attachment_service.proto`
  - `/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/instance_service.proto`
  - `/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/ai_service.proto`
  - `/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/shortcut_service.proto`
  - `/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/idp_service.proto`
  - `/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/common.proto`
- **`/bench/repo/proto/store/*.proto`** — internal storage message types (not the public surface).

How it becomes the public API surface:
- **Codegen config: `/bench/repo/proto/buf.gen.yaml`** compiles the protos into: Go structs (`protocolbuffers/go`), gRPC servers (`grpc/go`), Connect handlers (`connectrpc/go`), a **gRPC-Gateway REST layer** (`grpc-ecosystem/gateway`), an **OpenAPI spec** (`google-gnostic-openapi`), and TypeScript client types for the web frontend.
- **Generated code: `/bench/repo/proto/gen/api/v1/`** — contains `*.pb.go` (messages), `*_grpc.pb.go` (gRPC), and `*.pb.gw.go` (REST gateway) for each service.
- **Generated OpenAPI spec: `/bench/repo/proto/gen/openapi.yaml`**, embedded into the binary via `/bench/repo/proto/openapi_embed.go`. This is the REST API documentation, but it is derived from the protos — the protos are the true source.

Where the API is served/wired up:
- **`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/v1.go`** — `APIV1Service` implements all the generated gRPC service interfaces (`UnimplementedMemoServiceServer`, `UnimplementedUserServiceServer`, etc.) and `RegisterGateway` mounts both the gRPC-Gateway (REST) and Connect handlers onto an Echo HTTP server.
- Per-service Go implementations live alongside it in `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/` (e.g. `memo_service.go`, `reaction_service.go`, `idp_service.go`, `user_service_filter.go`, etc.).
- Additional public HTTP surfaces: **RSS** (`/bench/repo/server/router/rss/rss.go`), **MCP** (Model Context Protocol) server (`/bench/repo/server/router/mcp/`), a **file server** (`/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/`), and the **frontend** static router (`/bench/repo/server/router/frontend/frontend.go`).

Key dependencies confirming the stack (from `/bench/repo/go.mod`): `connectrpc.com/connect`, `github.com/grpc-ecosystem/grpc-gateway/v2`, `google.golang.org/grpc`, and `github.com/labstack/echo/v5` (HTTP router). No GraphQL, no tRPC.

**Bottom line:** There is no GraphQL schema. The public API is defined in Protocol Buffer files under `/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/`, exposed as gRPC + REST (gRPC-Gateway) + Connect, with an auto-generated OpenAPI document at `/bench/repo/proto/gen/openapi.yaml`, and served from `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/v1.go`.

**Actual API surface:** The public API is defined in **Protocol Buffer (`.proto`) files**, then exposed as **gRPC + REST (gRPC-Gateway) + Connect**, with a generated OpenAPI document.

- **Schema source of truth** — `proto/api/v1/*.proto`, one per service:
  - `proto/api/v1/memo_service.proto`, `user_service.proto`, `auth_service.proto`, `attachment_service.proto`, `instance_service.proto`, `ai_service.proto`, `shortcut_service.proto`, `idp_service.proto`, `common.proto`

- **Generated OpenAPI spec** — `proto/gen/openapi.yaml`, embedded via `proto/openapi_embed.go` (this is the closest thing to a "public API schema" document, but it's derived from the protos).
- **Where it's served/wired up** — `server/router/api/v1/v1.go` (`APIV1Service` implements the generated service interfaces and `RegisterGateway` mounts the REST + Connect handlers on Echo), with per-service implementations alongside it in `server/router/api/v1/`.
